import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 716

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/716](https://www.erdosproblems.com/716)
- [BES73] Brown, W. G. and Erdős, P. and S\'os, V. T., Some extremal problems on {$r$}-graphs.
  (1973), 53--63.
- [RuSz78] Ruzsa, I. Z. and Szemer\'{e}di, E., Triple systems with no six points carrying three
  triangles. Combinatorics (Proc. Fifth Hungarian Colloq., Keszthely, 1976), Vol. II (1978), 939-945.
-/

namespace Erdos716

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $3$-uniform hypergraphs with $6$ vertices and $3$ $3$-edges.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_3(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2)?$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa and Szemerédi [RuSz78] (this is known as the Ruzsa-Szemerédi
problem).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_716 :
    answer(True) ↔
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.configurationExtremalNumber n 3 6 3 : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos716

reformulations.difference: Rather than explicitly constructing the forbidden family of six-vertex, three-edge hypergraphs, configurationExtremalNumber excludes an edge family whenever some six-element vertex set contains at least three edges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Containment is non-induced in the source. From at least three edges inside a six-element set, choose exactly three distinct edges; these form a forbidden sub-hypergraph, with isolated vertices permitted. Conversely, any forbidden copy supplies six vertices containing at least three edges. The powersetCard/powerset enumeration consists exactly of all simple 3-uniform edge families on n vertices, so its maximum is the source’s extremal number. The containment equivalence and candidate-family characterization were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The original BES73 paper states the question using the forcing threshold f^(3)(n;6,3), whereas Lean uses the extremal maximum, as does erdosproblems.com.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: BES73 §1 defines f^(3)(n;6,3) as the extremal maximum plus one. Since the constant sequence 1 is o(n²), the forcing threshold is o(n²) if and only if the extremal maximum is o(n²). Thus the primary paper and the Lean declaration pose the same asymptotic question.

review.notes: The sole declaration is faithful. The source records an affirmative solution by Ruzsa and Szemerédi, consistent with answer(True) and research solved. Lean checks verified the ε–N interpretation, admissibility of the empty family, containment boundary cases, and extremal values 0,0,0,1,4,10,2 for n=0,…,6, without using the admitted theorem. RuSz78’s full text was not obtained; its attribution and result were corroborated by the problem page and Wikipedia. The reviewed file matches the committed version.
